strategyNarrative.introduction:
The National Roads Network is currently 21,292 km in total lane length, where 6,312 km is paved and 14,980 km is unpaved. Its functional classification is 12.2% Class A (All paved), 13.4% Class B (61% Paved), 73.7% Class C (12% Paved), and 0.7% is Class M (All Paved)

As noted in subsequent assessments, funding for national road maintenance has been insufficient over the years. There has been a major focus on upgrading roads from gravel to tarmac without matching the maintenance needs of the growth of the paved network. This means the road network gains across the country are being lost in a shorter time, as seen in the increased number of paved roads currently in poor condition (Appendix i: Photos). This has resulted in a huge maintenance backlog (Appendix ii).

The Current Asset Value (Depreciated Cost) of the National Roads and Bridges as of July 2024 was approximately 7.3 billion USD (26.9 trillion UGX), representing 5.6 billion USD (20.7 trillion UGX) of paved roads and 0.82 billion USD (3.0 trillion UGX) of unpaved roads. However, the replacement cost is about 10.2Bn USD (37.4Tn). This indicates an Asset loss of 10.5Tn. This loss is highly likely to accelerate upwards if no preventive maintenance of paved roads is undertaken within the next 3-5 years. We are currently undertaking an assessment, and progress is about 60% as of today.

International best practices of allocating road maintenance funds dictate that about 3.0% (306M USD or 1.1Trn UGX) of the Replacement Value each year should be allocated for preventive maintenance. Over the years however, allocation has been below 1.0% (70M USD or 260Bn UGX) of the value of the road network to maintenance each year. This year FY2025/26 has the same allocation albeit with a further deterioration. This allocation has only been enough to maintain about 24.5% of the national network in the previous years.

This lack of preventive maintenance measures has let paved roads slide to rehabilitation and reconstruction as a result. There has been not been any resealing or overlays done to prevent the roads from accelerated deterioration.
strategyNarrative.pavedConditionAssessment:
As of July 2025, the average paved-road condition index (VCI) stood at 77 %, placing the network in the “good” category. Of the 6,034 km assessed, 49.4% (2,980 km) were rated as Good and 24.9% (1,503 km) as Very Good, giving roughly three-quarters of the network a desirable condition. A further 22.8 % (1,377 km) were Fair, while only 2.9 % (174 km) fell into the Poor or Very Poor classes.

Rutting remains the most prevalent defect, affecting approximately 41 per cent (≈ 2,186 km) of the network in warning-to-severe condition. Other notable defects include ravelling (24%), all cracking (24%), wide cracking (19%), roughness (14%), and drainage deficiencies (10%). Approximately 193 km (3%) show moderate-to-severe potholing, while isolated potholes occur on an additional 928 km (15%).

When compared with FY 2023/24, roads in very good condition increased by 0.7 per cent and those in good condition by 4 %. However, fair sections deteriorated by 5%, and poor sections deteriorated by 2.3%. Due to reduced maintenance activity, ≈ approximately 220 km that previously required rehabilitation have now shifted to reconstruction. Current needs stand at approximately 260 km for rehabilitation and around 1,993 km for periodic maintenance, which has remained nearly constant year-over-year.
strategyNarrative.unpavedConditionAssessment:
As of July 2024, the Average Condition Index of unpaved roads was 59% which categorised the network as “fair”. This, however, was on the lower end of the fair rating, and as there have been no significant maintenance interventions undertaken for most of the remaining year, the network is in the poor category by now. Rutting was the most prominent defect with (72%) 9959 km in warning to severe condition, followed by Corrugations 6624 (48%), Erosion gullies is very common with almost 44% 6046 Km,28% of 3908 km with roughness, Gravel thickness ratings indicate the need for urgent regravelling on 11% 1511km, 0.3% 36km has no gravel and 10.7% 1474 km with gravel less than 50mm poor drainage condition both sides of the roads at (8%), poor formation levels at (9%).

Roads in very poor and poor condition have increased from 12% in 2024 to 19% in 2025. The roads in fair condition have decreased from 70% in 2024 to 65% in 2025. The condition of roads in good and very good condition has decreased from 18% in 2024 to 17% in 2025.

This brings the maintenance backlog to 80% of the unpaved network.
strategyNarrative.strategyApproach:
Under normal maintenance of paved roads, it is desirable to undertake preventive maintenance. It costs (USD 2,500-5,000/km) to undertake regular routine maintenance, (USD 51,000 – 100,000/km) for timely spot periodic maintenance, (USD/km 170,000 – 300000/km) for full periodic maintenance and (USD 600,000 - 700,000/km) for full rehabilitation. It is evident that for every delayed maintenance intervention, the cost at the next intervention level becomes exponential in a short time. It takes about 2-3 years for a road to fall from periodic maintenance to rehabilitation level, increasing the cost of intervention by about 4 times.

In order to eliminate the backlog of periodic maintenance, which stands at 1,993km for paved roads, there is an urgent need to undertake a series of preventive maintenance interventions. These shall mainly be resurfacing with Asphalt Concrete, Spot rehabilitation, Resealing and drainage improvements. These roads are exhibiting wide cracking, all cracking, moderate to warning roughness, and this requires periodic maintenance, light or heavy rehabilitation. It is proposed that the major international trade routes, especially the Northern corridor and its spurs, be placed under a long-term performance-based maintenance (OPRC) approach. This is in line with the best regional and global practices.
strategyNarrative.budgetForAdequateMaintenance: It shall require a commitment of about UGX 1.8Tn to remove the backlog of the 1,993km due for urgent periodic maintenance. A substantial number of the major corridors under this category require a long-term Output and performance-based contracting approach. On top of the ongoing 881km of roads under rehabilitation, we shall require another UGX 890Bn to work on the 344km that are due for rehabilitation and UGX 813Bn for 220km of reconstruction. We shall further require adequate commitment for the about 11,100km of unpaved roads (Roads with traffic volumes above 300 Vehicles per Day) that are already candidates for upgrade. This category requires increased periodic maintenance and shall be placed under a long-term framework or term maintenance contracting approaches to ensure they are motorable all year round.
